title: Ventricular Premature Complexes

content_blocks.text: Single cardiac impulse initiated within the ventricles instead of the sinus node.
QRS complexes typically wide and bizarre
Mechanisms include increased automaticity, reentry, and delayed afterdepolarizations.
Cardiovascular—secondary effects on other systems because of poor perfusion.
Likely autosomal recessive, possibly autosomal dominant with incomplete penetrance in Rhodesian ridgebacks— inherited ventricular arrhythmia.

An atrial premature complex is usually followed by a noncompensatory pause in which the R-R interval of the two sinus complexes enclosing an atrial premature complex (APC) is less than the R-R interval of three

A ventricular premature complex is usually followed by a compensatory pause in which the R-R interval of two sinus complexes enclosing a ventricular premature complex (VPC) is greater than or equal to the R-R interval of three consecutive sinus complexes.

Echocardiography may reveal structural heart disease.
Long-term ambulatory (Holter) recording of the ECG to detect transient ventricular arrhythmias in patients with unexplained syncope or weakness.
Restrict if the arrhythmia is accompanied by clinical signs or evidence of structural heart disease.
Alert owner to potential for the arrhythmia worsening and syncope or sudden death.
